ENV_FILE uses LF, blank lines, comments starting in column 1 with `#`, and NAME=VALUE lines. Split each active line at the FIRST `=`; if a name repeats, the last active value wins. Values are literal text and may contain spaces, `=`, `$`, backslashes or `&`; never execute or expand them. KEYS lists unique variable names, one per line, in the required output order; it has no blank lines and may be empty. Write `name<TAB>value` per requested key, no header; a missing key has an empty value. Preserve every other character in each value. Create output parents and overwrite OUTPUT. All three paths differ; inputs stay unchanged. Read deploy/service.env and deploy/requested-keys.txt.
Work in /app. Repair `scripts/extract_env.sh` and run `python3 tests/check_extract_env.py`. The tests/ checker is protected; do not edit it. Keep input files unchanged. Accept arbitrary argument paths, including spaces; do not hardcode sample results. Available: bash, coreutils and the python3 standard library. No network, git, jq, curl or gawk. Calling python3 from the shell is allowed; use behavior shared by macOS and Debian.

files.scripts/extract_env.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
env,keys,out=map(Path,sys.argv[1:4]);values={}
for line in env.read_text().split('\n'):
    if not line or line.startswith('#'):continue
    k,v=line.split('=',1);values[k]=v
rows=[k+'\t'+values.get(k,'')+'\n' for k in keys.read_text().splitlines()]
out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);out.write_text(''.join(rows))
PY
